minor.issue: FlashcardReview rows are NOT deleted when parent Flashcard is deleted. Model declares ondelete=CASCADE but SQLite ignores FK constraints unless `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` is set per connection (missing in /app/backend/core/database.py). Combined with SQLite ROWID reuse, orphan reviews cling to newly-created cards, corrupting a learner's SM-2 state (a fresh card can appear already 'learning' with next_review 1d out). This caused test_bulk_save_and_learner_review_flow to fail intermittently on repeat runs — passes on clean state, fails after 2nd iteration.

test_iteration22::test_authoring_status_admin_can_access asserts tutor_enabled/deep_research_enabled/flashcards_enabled are all False, but authoring.py flips them True in Iter 22/23/24 (expected per roadmap). This iter22 test is stale and should be updated to reflect the new expected shape.

action_items: Enable SQLite FK enforcement — in /app/backend/core/database.py add an @event.listens_for(engine, 'connect') hook that executes `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` when database_url starts with 'sqlite'. This turns the existing ondelete=CASCADE FKs into real cascades and prevents orphan FlashcardReview/AIJob rows from corrupting future data. (In Postgres this is already enforced.)

Alternatively (or additionally) — in routers/flashcards.py DELETE endpoint, explicitly `db.query(FlashcardReview).filter(flashcard_id==card_id).delete()` before deleting the Flashcard, so cleanup works regardless of DB engine.

Update /app/backend/tests/test_iteration22.py::test_authoring_status_admin_can_access to expect tutor_enabled=True, deep_research_enabled=True (when TAVILY_API_KEY present), flashcards_enabled=True. Currently a stale assertion left over from before Iter 22/23/24 flipped the flags.

Optional: Make test_iteration25::test_bulk_save_and_learner_review_flow use pytest addfinalizer/try-finally so the cleanup DELETE always runs even if an assertion fails mid-flight — reduces test-pollution risk.

rca of the issue: SM-2 E2E test failure RCA — sqlite3 default `PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF` means SQLAlchemy's `ForeignKey(..., ondelete='CASCADE')` declaration is not enforced at the DB level. When the admin DELETE cleanup ran at the end of a prior test, only the Flashcard row was removed; the FlashcardReview row for that card survived. SQLite additionally reuses the highest-deleted rowid on the next INSERT (no AUTOINCREMENT keyword), so the next bulk-save created a new Flashcard row that inherited the deleted card's id and, therefore, the orphan review. The learner's /due endpoint then filtered the 'new' card out because it saw a matching FlashcardReview scheduled 1 day in the future. Reproduction: run test_bulk_save_and_learner_review_flow twice in a row → 2nd run fails at `assert card_id in ids`. Mitigation options (in order of preference): (1) add `@event.listens_for(engine, 'connect')` in core/database.py to execute `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` for SQLite engines; (2) explicitly cascade-delete FlashcardReview rows in the router's DELETE handler; (3) switch the dev DB to Postgres (already supported via DATABASE_URL) where FKs are enforced by default.
